B2: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
If I had known, I would have called.
If I would know, I had called.
If I had knew, I would called.
A past counterfactual uses if + past perfect and would have + participle.
Choose the most precise conclusion.
A small volunteer study found an association between cycling and fewer sick days. It did not randomly assign participants.
Cycling guarantees perfect health.
The association is worth investigating, but causation is not established.
The study proves cycling has no effect.
An observational association does not establish a causal guarantee or prove no effect.
Complete: The proposal is practical, ___ it will require additional funding.
despite
although
because of
Although introduces a finite concessive clause.
What does the supplier offer?
We can deliver on Monday provided that you confirm the order by noon on Friday.
An unconditional Monday delivery
A Monday delivery conditional on timely confirmation
A guaranteed Friday delivery
Provided that introduces a necessary condition for this offer.
Choose the accurate reported form.
Yesterday the manager said, 'We are checking the figures.' Report this with backshift.
The manager said that they are check the figures.
The manager told that they checking the figures.
The manager said that they were checking the figures.
The requested backshift changes are checking to were checking.
Which summary preserves the comparison?
The exhibition's sound design is impressive, but its labels provide little historical context.
The review praises the sound but questions the contextual guidance.
The review rejects every aspect of the exhibition.
The review finds the labels historically comprehensive.
A mixed evaluation must retain both praise and reservation.
Choose the correct passive sentence.
The samples have tested yesterday.
The samples were tested yesterday.
The samples was testing yesterday.
Past-simple passive uses were tested with the plural subject.
What can be concluded?
The trial reduced journey times for bus passengers. The report did not measure effects on other road users.
Every road user benefited.
No road user benefited.
Bus passengers benefited; wider effects remain unmeasured.
The conclusion must preserve the measured population and the stated gap.
Choose the most constructive clarification.
A colleague asks for a report 'soon', but you have another urgent task.
Could you specify the deadline and which task takes priority?
I will assume soon means next month.
Your request is impossible and not worth discussing.
The question clarifies both deadline and priority without inventing either.
Complete: The evidence suggests the change ___ have contributed to the increase.
The evidence supports a possible contribution, not certainty.
must
might
cannot
Might expresses possibility without asserting necessity or impossibility.
Which criticism is justified?
A survey of fifty regular commuters is reported as 'the opinion of every resident'.
The headline generalises beyond the sample.
Fifty respondents necessarily represent everyone.
Commuters cannot have opinions.
The sampling group does not establish the views of all residents.
Choose the correct contrast.
Some prefer online study, whereas others value classroom discussion.
Some prefer online study, despite others value classroom discussion.
Some prefer online study, because of others value classroom discussion.
Whereas introduces a contrasting finite clause.
What is the speaker's position?
I support the aim, but I would prefer a pilot before a permanent policy.
Unconditional acceptance of immediate implementation
Rejection of the aim itself
Qualified support with a proposed trial
Support for the goal is qualified by a preference for testing implementation.
Choose the accurate deduction.
The office is empty, the lights are off and the last train has left. A strong past deduction is required.
They must have left.
They must left.
They have must leave.
Must have + participle expresses a strong deduction about a past event.
Which negotiation reply preserves the minimum requirement?
You need forty units for launch. The supplier offers thirty now and the rest later.
Thirty is enough even though we need forty.
If you can provide forty now, we can accept the balance later.
All future deliveries must be cancelled.
The counteroffer retains the minimum and offers flexibility on the remainder.
What does the statement establish?
The scheme aims to reduce demand by ten percent; full-year results are not yet available.
Ten percent is a measured annual saving.
Demand has certainly increased.
Ten percent is a target, not yet a confirmed annual result.
A target must not be silently converted into an observed outcome.
C1: Choose the correct inversion.
Rarely we have encountered such a contradiction.
Rarely have we encountered such a contradiction.
Rarely have encountered we such a contradiction.
A fronted negative adverb triggers subject-auxiliary inversion.
Which summary best calibrates the claim?
Retention improved at firms adopting flexible work, but management practices changed at the same time.
Flexible work alone guarantees retention.
Retention could not possibly have improved.
The improvement is observed, but its attribution to flexible work alone remains uncertain.
The observation is retained while its exclusive causal explanation is qualified.
Which response is diplomatic but explicit?
A senior colleague wants to publish unverified figures today.
I appreciate the deadline, but I cannot approve publication until the figures are verified.
Interesting; publish whatever you want.
Anyone who suggests that is incompetent.
Acknowledgement is combined with an explicit boundary and its condition.
What distinction reconciles these findings?
One study reports fewer interruptions for experienced remote staff. Another reports slower induction for remote newcomers.
Both measure exactly the same population and outcome.
The studies examine different groups and outcomes.
One must be false because remote work has only one possible effect.
Different populations and outcomes can support compatible observations.
Choose the most defensible criticism.
The announcement says 'difficulties were encountered' but names no responsible party or timetable.
The wording conclusively proves deliberate deception.
The absence of accountability is observable; a deceptive motive would need more evidence.
There are no identifiable omissions.
A textual omission is demonstrable, while a motive is an inference.
Complete: The findings are consistent ___ the proposed mechanism.
to
of
with
Consistent with expresses compatibility, not unique proof.
What does the reviewer object to?
The reviewer supports public data access but rejects the assertion that access alone guarantees research quality.
The sufficiency of access alone
Every form of data sharing
The existence of research
Support for a necessary or helpful component does not imply it is sufficient.
Choose the correct mixed conditional.
An unperformed past check affects what we know now.
If we would check yesterday, we had known now.
If we had checked, we would know now.
If we have checked, we would have know now.
Past perfect in the condition combines with a present conditional result.
Which plain-language explanation preserves the measurement limit?
The device reports a daily average, not the maximum concentration at each instant.
A low average guarantees no brief high values.
The device cannot answer any useful question.
The daily average may conceal brief peaks; those require more detailed measurements.
The reformulation preserves the scope without dismissing the device entirely.
What commitment is made?
We envisage a review in due course. No publication deadline has been agreed.
A review is intended, but no publication date is promised.
Publication before December is contractually guaranteed.
No review may ever take place.
Envisage expresses an intention, and in due course supplies no fixed date.
Choose the correct negative fronting.
By no means this is a complete explanation.
By no means is this a complete explanation.
By no means a complete explanation is this being.
Fronted by no means triggers inversion of is and this.
What should a synthesis retain?
Two authors support access, but one measures enrolment and the other meaningful participation after enrolment.
The distinction between entry and participation
A claim that the authors use identical measures
The assertion that one author opposes all access
Shared terminology does not erase a difference in operational meaning.
Which objection targets the actual dependency?
A proposal predicts savings but omits the staffing resources necessary to deliver them.
Savings can never occur in any organisation.
The prediction remains conditional on resources the budget does not provide.
The absent resources prove the projected savings already occurred.
The objection identifies an unprovided condition, not universal impossibility.
Choose the grammatically complete formal expression.
We are not yet in a position agree.
We are not yet a position to agreement.
We are not yet in a position to agree.
In a position to takes an infinitive.
What is the limit of one counterexample?
One poorly documented open dataset is found, in response to the claim that every open dataset guarantees high quality.
It defeats the universal guarantee, not every possible benefit of openness.
It proves all closed datasets are better.
It proves documentation never matters.
A counterexample refutes the universal claim without establishing its opposite universal.
Which summary is accurate for decision-makers?
A forecast gives a range of plausible outcomes rather than an exact prediction.
Promise the midpoint as a certainty.
Test whether the decision remains workable across the range.
Discard the range because uncertainty makes planning impossible.
Robust planning can use uncertainty without converting it into a guarantee.
C2: What is presupposed by this question?
When will the council finally admit that the experiment has failed?
Failure is already established and awaits admission.
The experiment has unquestionably succeeded.
No judgement of any kind is implied.
Finally admit frames failure as a settled truth rather than an argued proposition.
Which response resists the frame without evading evaluation?
The interviewer calls a mixed, partly unmeasured trial 'a disaster' before asking for an admission.
I will admit it next Tuesday.
Let us specify the criteria and distinguish missed, met and unmeasured outcomes.
All criticism is necessarily dishonest.
The response replaces the loaded premise with differentiated criteria.
How is the apparent praise functioning?
After three meetings without a decision, the chair calls the afternoon 'wonderfully decisive'.
As straightforward praise of a completed decision
As an exact statement of duration
As irony supported by the mismatch with events
The context contradicts the literal praise and supports an ironic reading.
Which paraphrase preserves scope?
The provider will not replace all damaged components.
Universal replacement is excluded; the covered subset still needs clarification.
No damaged component will ever be replaced.
Every essential component is guaranteed replacement.
Not all does not by itself identify a covered subset or mean none.
Why is 'refuted' too strong?
A response proposes an alternative explanation but supplies no decisive test between the two accounts.
Offering any alternative always proves the original false.
A challenge has been presented, not a demonstrated disproof.
Alternative explanations can never be discussed.
Refutation entails a stronger outcome than an unresolved counterproposal.
What does the word 'conceded' add?
A researcher volunteers a limitation at the outset; the summary says she later 'conceded' it.
A neutral guarantee of mathematical truth
No possible difference from acknowledged
A suggestion of reluctant yielding not established by the interview
Conceded can imply reluctance or retreat; the described context does not establish that.
Choose the faithful synthesis.
One historian studies legal change over a decade; another studies administrative continuity over a generation. They differ over interpretive priority.
Their observations may coexist, while a genuine disagreement about significance remains.
They agree about every interpretive issue.
They contradict each other on every possible fact.
Compatibility of observations does not erase competing judgements of significance.
What remains unresolved by aligning these forecasts?
One forecast assumes current policy; the other assumes the announced reforms are implemented.
Whether the forecasts have different conditions
Whether the reforms are credible and will be implemented
Whether conditions can affect forecasts
Reconciling assumptions does not establish the credibility of the conditional scenario.
Which revision preserves the review's meaning?
An intervention can work where capacity is sufficient; evidence from fragile settings is limited.
It works everywhere unless institutions are at fault.
It is proven ineffective in every fragile setting.
It may work with sufficient capacity; evidence in fragile settings remains limited.
The revision keeps both the enabling condition and the evidential gap without inventing blame.
Choose the correct emphatic construction.
What we need is an explicit criterion.
What we need are an explicit criterion.
What do we need is an explicit criterion.
The what-cleft uses a statement clause and a singular complement here.
What is being criticised?
Calling the payment a rescue rather than a subsidy changes the story of deservingness, but not its cost.
Any possibility of financial support
A rhetorical label substituting for a substantive justification
The arithmetic of a specified payment
The critique concerns framing, not a categorical objection to the payment.
Which explanation of cautious language is faithful?
The evidence is compatible with a mechanism but does not uniquely identify it.
The question is unimportant.
All mechanisms have been ruled out.
Certainty is limited by the evidence, not necessarily by the importance of the question.
Calibrated commitment follows the evidential limit without implying triviality.
Choose the exact contrast.
Several recommendations are approved, two need clarification and one is outside our remit.
Partial non-approval is not wholesale rejection of the report.
Every recommendation has been rejected.
The whole report has been unconditionally approved.
The account distinguishes approval, unresolved items and jurisdiction.
Complete: Absence of evidence should not be construed ___ evidence of fault.
with
as
of
Construe as means interpret as; the sentence warns against that substitution.
What makes this an understatement?
After a substantial, repeatedly documented delay, a member says, 'We may be slightly behind.'
The expression is stronger than the situation warrants.
The sentence supplies a precise duration.
The mild wording downplays the established extent of the delay.
Understatement expresses less intensity than the context supports.
Which compression is legitimate?
A public summary must be shorter, while retaining qualifications that affect the decision.
Remove incidental procedure, but retain the conclusion's scope and uncertainty.
Convert the central estimate into a guarantee.
Drop every exception so the sentence sounds confident.
Concision may remove incidental details without silently altering substantive qualifications.
